title: 📰 AI news · November 12
cta: 🔐 Check who can see my apps

items.title: 35,000 Grok-built apps open to everyone
items.text: Security firm Claroc found 35,578 of 37,571 checked apps built with Grok open to anyone: access "with the link" was the default. Inside were patient lab results and 18 plaintext passwords. If you build apps or bots with AI, anyone with the link may open yours too. Check the access settings of your apps and take passwords out of the code. Free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access": send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: Notion: AI chats leaked via a vendor
items.text: Notion's vendor Fireworks AI was breached, and AI chat transcripts from a small number of workspaces were exposed. Less than 1 percent of users are affected. Whatever you type to an AI assistant may sit with the service's vendor. Replace passwords and keys you pasted into AI chats.

items.title: AntiFox AI agents steal AWS keys
items.text: Arctic Wolf saw attackers run the open-source AntiFox on Alibaba Cloud servers: AI agents look for weak spots on websites, test stolen keys and take secrets from AWS clouds. A cloud key in your settings opens data like a password does. Open your AWS key list and disable the ones you don't need.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini Decision 1
items.text: A model for closed questions: yes or no, multiple choice, scale ratings. It handles up to 1,000 questions in one pass across text, images, audio, video and PDFs, answers in 150–250 milliseconds, $0.10 per million input tokens.

items.title: DeepL translates intonation
items.text: The Aure model in DeepL Voice carries tone, emotion, emphasis and speaking pace into the translation. Eight languages; works in online meetings, in-person conversations and the API.

items.title: AI verified Signal's encryption in 4 weeks
items.text: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code mathematically proves software meets its security specs. Signal's cryptographic core was verified in four weeks instead of years: agents wrote over 6 million lines of proof.

takeaway: Today data and keys again sit where defaults leave them: an open link, chats at a vendor, a key in cloud settings. Recommendation: check who can open your apps and bots, and remove passwords and extra keys from them.
